title: Strengthening FIU cooperation: AMLA hosts Interoperability Working Group for EU FIUs

paras.text: Interoperability as a foundation for cooperation

Effective cooperation between FIUs depends on information being exchanged securely and efficiently across the Union. FIU.net, the secure platform connecting EU FIUs, can deliver its full potential only if it operates effectively alongside the diverse national systems used by FIUs. Discussions focused on technical requirements, opportunities and challenges, as well as the implications of the EU's new anti-money laundering framework for both national systems and FIU.net.
A shared priority for the FIU community

In her opening address, Executive Board Member Hennie Verbeek-Kusters stressed that interoperability is a priority for the entire FIU community, regardless of the technical environment used by individual FIUs. She emphasised that AMLA does not seek to promote one system model over another. Instead, its objective is to help all national systems connect effectively with FIU.net in support of cross-border cooperation.

Looking ahead to the transfer of FIU.net to AMLA, she noted that AMLA will place particular emphasis on the practical experience of FIUs and remains committed to working closely with them on the platform's future development.
Supporting, strengthening and connecting EU FIUs

Hosting the meeting forms part of AMLA's work under FIUnion, the framework designed to support, strengthen and connect the EU's FIUs. More seamless interaction between national systems and FIU.net reduces administrative burdens and allows FIUs to focus more of their resources on analysis and the fight against illicit finance. AMLA looks forward to continuing this work together with the FIU community.

Interoperability is not simply a technical issue. It has a direct impact on how effectively FIUs can cooperate in practice. Our objective is to help ensure that national systems and FIU.net work together in ways that support cooperation rather than create unnecessary obstacles, allowing FIUs to focus their efforts on analysing and combating financial crime.
